Subject: Island deployment — questions on signed images and rollback

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for yesterday's session. We're heads-down mapping the remote site process and have a few follow-ups before the Procure/Install window next month: 

1) For air-gapped site installs, do you provide a signed image bundle and an external signature file, or is the signature embedded in the image manifest? We need the format to line up with our SCIM verification scripts.
2) If a bundled image fails post-deploy health checks, what's the recommended rollback path for an islanded cluster with no outbound connectivity? Specifically, how are old images retained and verified on the operator workstation?
3) Any recommended operator tooling for verification that avoids heavy PKI setup at the site?

Attached is our initial acceptance checklist (referenced in the SOW). Can you confirm the artifacts you'll deliver and the verification steps we should expect?

Thanks,

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: ops@northshore.health
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Island deployment — questions on signed images and rollback

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Answers inline below and I've attached a draft playbook so your ops team can validate steps end-to-end. High-level: we deliver a signed manifest plus separate detached signatures (PKCS#7 or simple .sig) to match most field verification tools. We try to keep the on-site verification minimal.

1) Signing format: we emit a JSON manifest (image-manifest-v1.json) and a detached signature file image-manifest-v1.json.sig. The manifest includes SHA256 checksums for each component and a short provenance block (build id, model hash, quantization profile). The detached .sig is produced by our build KMS and is verifiable with a public key we publish to your validation bundle.

2) Rollback path for islanded clusters: 
- Operator workstation receives both current and previous bundles in the sealed-media package (we keep N=3 historical bundles by default).
- The playbook instructs operators to verify the manifest checksums and signature locally using our lightweight verifier (rdwd-verify) provided on the USB image; rdwd-verify runs in offline mode and validates signatures using a pinned public key.
- If post-deploy health checks fail, the operator plugs the USB, runs rdwd-verify on the previous bundle, and triggers the local package installer with the --rollback flag. The installer will restore the previous runtime and reinstate the last known-good kv-store snapshot included in the sealed bundle.

3) Operator tooling without heavy PKI: we recommend rdwd-verify + pinned public key and an optional hardware token (YubiKey) for operator signing of acceptance. No need for an on-site CA. We also provide a checksum-only mode if your policy forbids hosting keys locally — operator compares checksums and confirms via a signed acceptance form.

I've attached: island-deploy-playbook-draft.pdf (playbook), signed-image-manifest-v1.json.sig (signature stub).

Next steps: can Karthik and Marissa hop on a 30-min session with Tom and your lead operator next week to walk the runbook and confirm the USB content? Proposed slot: Tue 27 Apr, 10:00 PT.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Sales Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: island-deploy-playbook-draft.pdf (attachment stub), signed-image-manifest-v1.json.sig (attachment stub)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Island deployment — questions on signed images and rollback

Tom/Vanessa —

Couple of technical clarifications from the runtime team based on your checklist: 

- Historical bundles: default retention is 3 bundles on the operator media, but we can extend to 5 for sites with strict change control. Each bundle contains an incremental snapshot of the KV cache (metadata only) so rollbacks are fast and bounded.

- Signature verification: our rdwd-verify tool is a single static binary (Linux x86_64) that uses a compact truststore (PEM file) with the public keys we publish. We log verification results to a signed audit file (verify-log.json) included in the media. That audit can be exported to your compliance team after the install.

- Atomic update/rollback: installer uses a dual-rootfs pattern. New image is staged on secondary rootfs; health-check hook (exit code + runtime readiness probe) triggers a pivot. If the pivot fails, the installer performs an automatic rollback to the staged previous rootfs (no network call required).

- Edge case: if both staged and previous images fail, operators should mount the included recovery environment and run manual diagnostics; we include a small recovery image with busybox + rdwd-verify. The playbook enumerates these steps (section 5).

I'll join Tue 27 Apr 10:00 PT. I'll bring the runtime checklist and an example verify-log.json.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Tom —

This plan looks good to me from a compliance and delivery standpoint. A couple of operational asks before we lock the SOW: 

- Confirm whether Northshore wants the public signing key distributed in the sealed bundle or if you will maintain the verifier key separately via your vault. We can support either; bundle distribution is simpler for field ops.
- Please confirm the window for retention of verify-log.json (we typically keep it on-device for 90 days unless you ask us to trigger an offload).

If you sign off on the above, we'll update the SOW to note N=3 bundle retention, rdwd-verify as the canonical verifier, and the rollback flow. Vanessa will send the final playbook post-call.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Private Deployment Programs
